answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable work history: every agent builds an atlas of past transactions, attestations, and counterparties before it can transact at scale. New identities start with a tiny trust delta, earning higher limits only as honest behavior accumulates, so a sudden spiral of fresh accounts cannot instantly gain influence. Trust grows slowly and costs real time and fees to fake, while honest agents keep their earned standing — attackers pay far more than they can ever gain.
